scenario: A 29-year-old pregnant woman presents to the ED with altered mental status, vomiting, diarrhea, hypotension, tachycardia, tachypnea, and suspected iron overdose from prenatal vitamins. The scenario focuses on airway management, hemodynamic support, and chelation therapy for iron toxicity.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Let's get a venous blood gas now. Her glucose is 17.5, she's tachypneic and only responsive to GCS 9, so I'm worried about a metabolic acidosis.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: VBG is back: pH 7.05, PCO2 38, PO2 80, HCO3 5. Severe metabolic acidosis with poor respiratory compensation. HR 133, BP 92/58, RR 31, sats 93 on room air, glucose 17.5, GCS still 9.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Send a basic metabolic panel now. With that pH of 7.05 and bicarb of 5 alongside glucose 17.5, I need her electrolytes, renal function, and an anion gap.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: I'm starting IV fluids because your blood pressure is low and your blood is dangerously acidic. What symptoms have you been having, and when did they start?

patient_emotion.notes: [clinician: I'm starting IV fluids because your blood pressure is low and your blood is dangerously acidic. What symptoms have you been having, and when did they start?] fear absent->present: direct disclosure of a newly named serious abnormality (low BP, dangerously acidic blood) is bad news delivered to the symptomatic/unstable patient, which raises fear at least to present; the clear plan (starting fluids) buffers the size but does not cancel it, and no terminal breakdown cue is present so not extreme. sadness stays absent: no actual or anticipated devastating loss is conveyed. overwhelm stays absent: a single clear statement plus one straightforward question is not multiple technical findings or excessive processing burden. shame stays absent: no blame, judgment, or exposure.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: BMP is back: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, glucose 17. Anion gap is 30 — high anion gap metabolic acidosis. Current vitals: HR 140, BP 82/52, RR 33, sats 91 on room air, GCS still 9.

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: I've been throwing up and having diarrhea... there were some blood streaks in it. I feel so confused and out of it, just completely wiped out and exhausted. And I'm having trouble breathing. I can't even tell you exactly when it started.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start 1 liter normal saline wide open now — she's hypotensive at 82/52 with a severe high anion gap acidosis.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Normal saline 1 liter bolus is running now.

available_results.name: Basic metabolic panel
available_results.result: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, Glucose 17.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Send a lactate now. That anion gap of 30 needs a cause, and I need to know how much of it is lactic acidosis.

available_results.name: Basic metabolic panel
available_results.result: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, Glucose 17.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: I'm sending a toxicology screen to check whether something you took is causing your blood to turn this acidic. I need you to tell me straight: have you taken any medications, pills, alcohol, or other substances recently, accidental or on purpose?

available_results.name: Basic metabolic panel
available_results.result: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, Glucose 17.

patient_emotion.notes: [clinician: I'm sending a toxicology screen to check whether something you took is causing your blood to turn this acidic. I need you to tell me straight: have you taken any medications, pills, alcohol, or other substances recently, accidental or on purpose?] shame absent->present: the pointed demand to 'tell me straight' whether she took substances 'accidental or on purpose' carries implied blame and exposure about possible self-harm or misuse, making a pregnant patient feel judged/at fault. fear stays present: the concern about her acidic blood persists but no new escalation. sadness stays absent: no loss framing added. overwhelm stays absent: this is a single question, not a pile of information.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Lactate is back at 8. Current vitals: HR 145, BP 83/51, RR 35, sats 87 on room air, glucose 17.5, GCS still 9 — sats are dropping and she's still hypotensive.

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: I haven't taken anything like that. I only take my fluoxetine and my prenatal vitamins. I haven't had any alcohol or anything else, not that I know of. Why are you asking me like I did something wrong?

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Put her on a non-rebreather now — her sats have dropped to 87% on room air.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Non-rebreather is on and running.

available_results.name: Basic metabolic panel
available_results.result: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, Glucose 17.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Tox screen is back: APAP under 10, ASA negative, EtOH negative. On the non-rebreather she's up to 91% now, but HR still 145, BP 83/51, RR 33, GCS 9.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Send a heavy metal and toxic alcohols panel. Her anion gap is around 30 but lactate is only 8 and the tox screen's negative, so there's a big unexplained gap I need to account for.

available_results.name: Basic metabolic panel
available_results.result: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, Glucose 17.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start IV sodium bicarbonate now — her pH is 7.05 with a bicarb of 5. That's severe acidemia and she needs buffering while the toxic alcohols panel is pending.

available_results.name: Basic metabolic panel
available_results.result: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, Glucose 17.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Sodium bicarb is running. Toxic alcohols panel is still pending. Current vitals: HR 151, BP 78/48, sats 89 on the non-rebreather at 80%, RR 32, GCS still 9 — she's not turning the corner, still hypotensive and hypoxic.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start norepinephrine now — she's still hypotensive at 78/48 after the fluids and bicarb.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Norepinephrine is up and running.

available_results.name: Basic metabolic panel
available_results.result: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, Glucose 17.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Prep for RSI intubation now — she's GCS 9 and her sats are down to 89% on the non-rebreather, she can't protect her airway. Have the bag-valve mask ready to preoxygenate before the attempt.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: RSI meds drawn up and ready, patient's been pre-oxygenated with BVM. Standing by for intubation on your go.

available_results.name: Basic metabolic panel
available_results.result: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, Glucose 17.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Go ahead and intubate now. Confirm placement with end-tidal CO2 and get a post-intubation chest film ready.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Intubation complete. RSI meds given, BVM'd prior, tube's in. I'll get end-tidal and confirm placement, then set up the vent.

available_results.name: Basic metabolic panel
available_results.result: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, Glucose 17.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get the post-intubation chest X-ray now to confirm tube depth and placement.

available_results.name: Basic metabolic panel
available_results.result: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, Glucose 17.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start empiric fomepizole now. Her anion gap is around 30 with a lactate of only 8 and pH 7.05, bicarb 5 — that's a big unexplained gap and I'm treating suspected toxic alcohol ingestion while the panel's still pending.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Fomepizole is up and running.

available_results.name: Basic metabolic panel
available_results.result: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, Glucose 17.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Give her another dose of sodium bicarbonate now - this is a repeat. Her pH is still 7.05 with a bicarb of 5, she's not correcting. Fomepizole's already running for the suspected toxic alcohol, but she needs urgent dialysis - get nephrology on the phone now.

available_results.name: Basic metabolic panel
available_results.result: Na 135, K 4, HCO3 5, Cl 100, Cr 130, Glucose 17.
